sights.w: Encyclopedic art museum on Museum Mile with over 1.5 million works spanning 5,000 years, from Egyptian temples to European masters.
sights.k: Pay-what-you-wish only for NY State residents; others pay a fixed admission. Closed Wednesdays.

sights.w: 843-acre landscaped park by Olmsted and Vaux running from 59th to 110th Street, with Bethesda Terrace, the Ramble, and the Reservoir loop.
1931 Art Deco skyscraper with 86th and 102nd floor observatories offering 360-degree views across the city and beyond.
sights.k: Timed tickets recommended; sunset slots sell out. Open late, past 11pm.

sights.w: Open-air observation deck atop Rockefeller Center with an unobstructed head-on view of the Empire State Building and Central Park.
sights.k: Entrance is on West 50th Street between Fifth and Sixth Avenues.

sights.address: Gansevoort Street & Washington Street, New York, NY 10014
sights.w: 1.45-mile elevated park built on a former freight rail viaduct, running through Chelsea past gardens, art installations, and city views.
sights.k: Southern entrance at Gansevoort St has elevator access. Free.

sights.w: 1913 Beaux-Arts rail terminal with a celestial-mural ceiling over the Main Concourse and the acoustic Whispering Gallery by the Oyster Bar ramp.
sights.k: Stand in opposite corners of the tiled archway to hear a whisper across the vault.

sights.n: New York Public Library, Stephen A. Schwarzman Building
sights.w: 1911 Beaux-Arts main branch guarded by the marble lions Patience and Fortitude, home to the vast third-floor Rose Main Reading Room.
sights.k: Free entry; Rose Reading Room open Monday to Saturday.

sights.address: 99 Margaret Corbin Drive, New York, NY 10040
sights.w: The Met's branch for medieval European art in Fort Tryon Park, built from parts of five French cloisters and home to the Unicorn Tapestries.
sights.k: Far uptown in Washington Heights; admission is included with a Met ticket.

sights.w: Greenwich Village square anchored by the Washington Arch and a central fountain, a longtime hub for street performers, chess, and NYU life.
sights.k: Free; liveliest on warm weekend afternoons.

sights.w: Henry Clay Frick's Gilded Age mansion showing Old Master paintings by Vermeer, Rembrandt, and Bellini; reopened April 2025 after a major renovation.
sights.k: The mansion's second floor is now open to the public for the first time.

sights.w: J.P. Morgan's 1906 private library in Murray Hill, with a three-tier tapestry-hung study and holdings from Gutenberg Bibles to literary manuscripts.
sights.k: Closed Mondays; the historic library rooms are the highlight.

sights.w: Restored 19th-century tenement telling immigrant stories through recreated apartments; entry is only by guided tour from the visitor center.
sights.k: Tours must be booked; the museum interior is not open for free walk-ins.

sights.w: Hidden one-acre park perched 40 feet above the Financial District, with a lawn, boardwalk, and East River views over the Brooklyn Bridge.
sights.k: Reach it via an easy-to-miss escalator set back from Water Street.

sights.w: Free Washington Heights museum with the finest collection of Spanish art outside Spain, including Goya, El Greco, and Sorolla's Vision of Spain murals.
sights.k: Free timed ticket required as of January 2026.

sights.address: 555 Edgecombe Avenue, Apt 3F, New York, NY 10032
sights.w: Free living-room jazz concert held every Sunday since 1993 in a Sugar Hill apartment, run by pianist Marjorie Eliot and family.
sights.k: Sundays at 3pm; doors around 2:30pm. Free, donations welcome; arrive early for a seat.

sights.address: City Hall Station, New York, NY 10007
sights.w: Ornate 1904 station with Guastavino-tiled vaults and skylights, closed to service since 1945; NY Transit Museum runs occasional member tours.
sights.k: No regular access; you can glimpse it by staying on a downtown 6 train past the Brooklyn Bridge stop as it loops.

food.address: 205 East Houston Street, New York, NY 10002
food.w: Cash-and-ticket Lower East Side deli open since 1888, serving 15,000 lbs of pastrami a week under old neon and salami-hanging signs.

food.dish: classic New York plain cheese slice
food.w: Greenwich Village slice institution since 1975, turning out thin, foldable New York-style plain slices from a stand-up counter until the early hours.
Chinatown counter for Xi'an-style hand-pulled biang biang noodles and cumin lamb, grown from a Flushing basement stall into a beloved local chain.

food.dish: bagel with lox and cream cheese
food.address: 179 East Houston Street, New York, NY 10002
food.w: Family-run appetizing shop since 1914, slicing smoked salmon, whitefish, and sable behind the counter of a landmark Lower East Side storefront.

food.dish: adobada pork taco with grilled pineapple
food.w: Chelsea Market taco stand griddling adobada pork shaved from a trompo onto hand-pressed tortillas; standing-room only and near-constant lines.
1885 Garment District chophouse famous for its mammoth mutton chop, dry-aged steaks, and ceilings hung with thousands of clay churchwarden pipes.
Original Upper West Side basement bakery known for its thick, gooey-centered six-ounce chocolate chip walnut cookies baked to order.

food.address: 328 Malcolm X Boulevard, New York, NY 10027
food.w: Harlem soul food landmark founded by Sylvia Woods in 1962, serving fried chicken, braised oxtails, and cornbread with weekend gospel brunch.
